Standardised causal-style contrast for a binary treatment

Source: R/verb-estimate.R
estimate.Rd

Estimates a covariate-adjusted marginal contrast between the two levels of a binary treatment by G-computation (outcome standardisation): a survival model is fitted for Surv(time, status) ~ treatment * (confounders), every subject's outcome is predicted under both treatment levels, and the counterfactual mean survival curves are contrasted.

Usage

estimate(
  formula,
  data,
  model,
  estimand = c("RMST_diff", "RMST_ratio", "survival_diff", "survival_ratio"),
  treatment,
  tau,
  times = NULL,
  spec = list(),
  R = 200,
  conf = 0.95,
  refit = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A survival formula whose right-hand side lists the confounders (the treatment is added by the function, with treatment-by-confounder interactions).

data

A data frame.

model

A learner id (list_survlearners()$learner) or a custom learner (see fit()).

estimand

One of "RMST_diff" (default), "RMST_ratio", "survival_diff", "survival_ratio".

treatment

Name of a binary column in data. The larger value is the "treated" (A = 1) level.

tau

Horizon: the RMST restriction time for the RMST estimands, or the evaluation time for the survival estimands.

times

Prediction grid; NULL picks up to 50 event-time quantiles (5th to 95th percentile). Must reach tau.

spec

Engine arguments for the learner (named list).

R

Bootstrap replicates (default 200).

conf

Confidence level (default 0.95).

refit

Logical; refit the model inside each bootstrap replicate (default TRUE).

seed

Optional RNG seed.

...

Unused.

Value

A survalis_estimate object with estimand, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, conf, treatment, levels, tau, R, refit, boot (replicate estimates) and curves (counterfactual mean survival for each arm on times).

Details

Uncertainty is a nonparametric bootstrap over subjects; by default the model is refitted in each replicate (refit = TRUE), which propagates model estimation error. Set refit = FALSE for a faster interval that is conditional on the fitted model.

Interpretation

The estimate has a causal reading only under standard identification assumptions: consistency, no unmeasured confounding given the formula covariates, positivity, no interference, and a correctly specified outcome model. For a non-manipulable attribute it is a covariate-adjusted marginal contrast, not a causal effect. This is a plug-in G-formula estimator; it is not doubly robust.

Examples

est <- estimate(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran,
                model = "coxph", estimand = "RMST_diff",
                treatment = "trt", tau = 300, R = 50, seed = 1)
est
#> <survalis_estimate> RMST difference at tau = 300  (model: coxph)
#>   treatment: trt  (2 vs 1)
#>   estimate: -14.3905   95% CI [-40.6135, 7.8719]   (50 bootstrap, refit)
#>   plug-in G-formula; causal reading needs exchangeability, positivity,
#>   consistency, no interference and a correct outcome model.
